text:
Alice (Support): hey team, acme reported a sudden p99 spike for requests hitting orca-extended-2b after we onboarded the tokenizer changes last night. p95 also up ~2x. customer says it started ~01:10 UTC and affects long-context workloads (~8k tokens). link to their sample: https://acme.example/samples/req-9832
Ben (Eng Runtime): thanks alice. can you paste p95/p99 numbers and an example header+payload? any correlation with model variant or host region?
Alice (Support): p95 baseline was 120ms -> 230ms, p99 baseline 450ms -> 1.6s. sample headers:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer ****
X-Model: orca-extended-2b-v1.1
Content-Type: application/json
```
payload includes prompt length ~6.2k tokens (after tokenization). they say short prompts fine.
Claire (Eng ML): if short prompts are fine and long ones regress, suspect tokenizer delta that changes tokenization boundary or increases token count, or a kv-cache cold miss pattern. did we change bpe merges? which tokenizer commit onboarded?
Alice (Support): onboarding PR #3124 merged 2026-02-28 by @mike. PR title: "orca-tokenizer: add cjk normalization + bpe merge heuristics".
Ben (Eng Runtime): also check runtime kernel changes. We rolled a micro-optimization yesterday afternoon that touched attention indexing for sequences >4096. Deploy Bot: canary deploy 2026-03-02T18:40 UTC: runtime/v3.14.2 -> v3.14.3.
Derek (Oncall): I saw p99 alerts for longctx@prod around the same timeframe. I already pinned a few dedicated pools to fallback-model=orca-extended-2b-quantized to take pressure off.
Claire (Eng ML): quick repro idea: run tokenizer on a canonical set and diff token counts between v1.0 and v1.1. also try running a synthetic workload with continuous attention to see KV cache reuse.
Ben (Eng Runtime): repro steps i'm thinking:
1) curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Model: orca-extended-2b-v1.1" -d @longprompt.json 
2) measure server-side compute (nvlink GPU time) and tail latency.
Add env var LOG_KV_CACHE=1 to catch cache hits/misses in logs.
Alice (Support): acme shared server logs showing lots of token-split warnings:
```
[warn] tokenizer: fallback_split: applied aggressive split for input chunk idx=14 original_len=512 -> split_count=3
[info] runtime: kv_cache_miss seq_id=3412 evicted_prefix=0
```
Emma (Product): (not in channel) but fyi customer is on a paid dedicated contract and asked for temporary SLA credit if we don't mitigate within 24h.
Ben (Eng Runtime): that tokenizer fallback_split log is suspicious. aggressive splitting increases request length after tokenization which can push sequence lengths >4096 into the slow code path. Claire, does v1.1 change splitting heuristics?
Claire (Eng ML): yes v1.1 enabled "aggressive_chunking" for CJK heavy prompts to improve semantic splits. It reduces semantic boundary errors but increases token count in some pathological cases. We didn't expect this to affect KV cache behavior this severely.
Derek (Oncall): ops data: long-run GPU occupancy for affected requests jumps from 45% -> 92% and GPU mem spikes around token 4200, causing context-switching overhead.
Ben (Eng Runtime): timeline hypothesis: tokenizer change -> increased token count -> more requests hitting long-sequence attention path -> runtime v3.14.3 has a regression for strided attention perf past 4096 which amplifies p99. Deploy Bot: canary telemetry shows 3% higher p99 for sequences >4096 on v3.14.3 vs v3.14.2.
Alice (Support): customer asked for workaround. suggested immediate options?
Claire (Eng ML): quick mitigations: 
- roll back aggressive_chunking in tokenizer for orca-extended-2b to v1.0 behavior (fast to revert at model serving config layer)
- add an on-the-fly token truncation/clipping policy for requests marked "non-critical-quality"
- expose a model variant map that routes long-context requests to the older tokenizer/model combo or quantized variant until patch is validated.
Ben (Eng Runtime): ops mitigations: 
- rollback runtime v3.14.3 on canary and hold further rollouts (I can do this now)
- enable a temporary route policy: if token_count_post_tokenizer > 4500 then route to fallback-pool (quantized variant) and set header X-Fallback-Reason = longctx-heuristic
Derek (Oncall): i'll open an incident and set priority. running rollback on canary now. i'm also throttling worst offenders (per-customer tail-rate limiting).
Deploy Bot: rollback triggered: runtime/v3.14.3 -> v3.14.2 on canary (id: canary-12). Estimated completion: 6m.
Ben (Eng Runtime): good. after rollback we should re-run synthetic long-context load vs both tokenizer versions. Claire can we run token diffs + synthetic perf?
Claire (Eng ML): on it. initial diff on 100 sample prompts: median token count increased 9% with aggressive_chunking; worst-case +-32%. starting synthetic run now (longseq harness: 8k tokens, concurrency 20).
[~20m later]
Claire (Eng ML): synthetic run results: with v1.1 tokenizer + runtime v3.14.2 p99 = 1.3s; with v1.0 tokenizer + runtime v3.14.2 p99 = 0.48s. with v1.1 + runtime v3.14.3 p99 = 1.8s. so both tokenizer and runtime regressed, but runtime patch amplifies the effect.
Ben (Eng Runtime): clear. plan: immediate rollback of runtime rollout (stop), short-term revert tokenizer on model-serving config for orca-extended-2b, and create an automated routing rule to direct >4500 token requests to quantized fallback. longer-term: revert kernel change + fix strided attention perf and add integration test for tokenization delta impact.
Alice (Support): notified acme of mitigation plan and ETA ~1.5h. they asked for a temporary traffic-shaping rule instead of full revert; said they'd prefer quality preserved.
Eva (Product): note for contract: if we route them to quantized fallback, quality might degrade slightly. let's offer them a report and optionally credit on SLA if we cannot deliver original quality within 24h.
Derek (Oncall): action items:
- Ben: stop rollout + validate canary rollback (in progress) -> due 15m
- Claire: revert tokenizer for orca-extended-2b on serving config and run tokenization A/B tests -> due 45m
- Ben/Derek: add routing rule to fallback pool for token_count > 4500 and apply temporary per-customer tail-rate limiting -> due 30m
- Alice: communicate to customer and capture their reaction/acceptance -> due 15m
- Ben: create perf regression PR + integration test for longseq attention path -> due EOD
Deploy Bot: canary rollback complete.
Ben (Eng Runtime): confirmed canary p99 back to baseline on recent runs. rolling hold placed on v3.14.3. I'll start a revert PR for the attention index optimization and add stress test for >4096 sequences.
Claire (Eng ML): tokenizer revert applied on model-serving config; A/B shows p99 for the customer traffic dropped back to 520ms. pushing config change to prod after validation.
Alice (Support): customer accepted temporary routing to quantized variant for a few hours while we finish validation. they appreciate fast response :thumbsup:
Eva (Product): i'll draft a short postmortem blurb and SLA note. we should call out interplay between tokenizer heuristics and runtime kernel changes as a root cause.
Derek (Oncall): incident ticket #INC-2026-118 opened and linked to this thread. marking as high priority.
Ben (Eng Runtime): final notes: add metric for token_count_post_tokenizer in request pipeline so we can alert earlier. also add synthetic daily longseq run as a canary job.
Alice (Support): thanks all. i'll update acme and close loop. will follow up with postmortem once root cause writeup is ready. :heavy_check_mark:
